issues.description: Method name mismatch in Exercise 1: the template defines a method named build_grover(...) but the class run() method calls grover_circuit(...). The problem statement and the solution implementation expect a grover_circuit-style entry point. This naming inconsistency will cause AttributeError / confusion for students when following the run() example or tests that expect grover_circuit.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the template and run() method consistent: rename the template method build_grover(...) to grover_circuit(...) (matching the problem statement/tests and the solution), or change run() to call build_grover(...). Ensure the method name used in run(), tests, and documentation all match the method provided in the template.

issues.description: The template defines a method named build_grover(...) but the class run() calls self.grover_circuit(...); the solution implements grover_circuit(...). This mismatch between 'build_grover' (template) and 'grover_circuit' (solution and run invocation) refers to the same conceptual operation (constructing the Grover circuit) with different identifiers, creating a direct mapping and runtime confusion for students.
issues.suggestedFix: Rename the template method build_grover(...) to grover_circuit(...) so the method name matches the run() invocation and the solution reference; alternatively, change the run() call to self.build_grover(...) and update the solution accordingly. Prefer using grover_circuit(...) across template, tests, and solution for consistency.
